Zakat, taken from the rich for the poor, ranks with worship and prayer among deeds leading to Paradise; Abu Bakr vowed to fight anyone withholding it, and Umar agreed.
Unpaid Zakat returns on Judgement Day as trampling animals and a snake; paying it purifies wealth, none is due below set amounts, and Abu Dhar warned hoarders.
No Zakat is due below five camels, uqiyas or wasqs; Abu Bakr's letter allows another camel age with adjustment and bars combining or splitting herds; women gave ornaments at Eid.
Abu Bakr's letter set Zakat on camels, sheep and silver, refusing old or defective animals; he would fight over a withheld goat; Mu'adh was to spare people's best property.
No Zakat is due on a Muslim's horse or slave.
Told three men refused Zakat, the Prophet faulted Ibn Jamil, whom Allah made rich, excused Khalid, whose armour was kept for Allah's cause, and said Al-Abbas owes it double.
A tenth is due on rain-watered land, a twentieth on well-watered land, none below five wasqs; the Prophet took a charity date from Al-Hasan's or Al-Husain's mouth.
Mu'adh was sent to call the People of the Scripture to Allah, prayer and Zakat, sparing their best property and fearing the oppressed's curse; the Prophet blessed those bringing alms.
No compensation is due for one killed by an animal, a well or a mine, but a fifth is due on Rikaz; the Prophet checked his Zakat collector's accounts.
Bringing a newborn for Tahnik, Anas found the Prophet branding the Zakat camels.
Zakat-ul-Fitr: one Sa' of dates, barley, raisins or other food for every Muslim, free, slave, young or old, before the Eid prayer; later people substituted half a Sa' of wheat.
Abu Bakr's written law of zakat says partners in jointly owned sheep pay its zakat equally.
Ali sends his son with a document of the Prophet's rules on charity to Uthman for his Zakat officials, and Uthman declines it.
Wealth whose zakat is unpaid will become a bald poisonous snake on the Day of Resurrection, coiling round its owner's neck and biting his cheeks.
Hoarded wealth with unpaid zakat will appear as a bald snake; Abu Dhar said the hoarding verse covers Muslims too, and Ibn Umar said zakat later purified wealth.
Abu Bakr's letter forbade merging or splitting property to avoid Zakat, treasure whose Zakat is unpaid becomes a snake on Resurrection Day, and some people allowed tricks to escape it.
